name: Competitive Intelligence
description: Build a source-dated, buyer-centered competitive picture without laundering marketing claims into facts.

tasks.name: Frame the competitive question
tasks.objective: Define decision, market boundary, competitors/alternatives, segment, geography, time horizon, and evidence needed. Distinguish direct competitors, substitutes, and status quo.

tasks.name: Collect primary competitive evidence
tasks.objective: Gather public product docs, pricing, demos, changelogs, job postings, filings, customer reviews, sales feedback, win-loss, app/traffic signals, patents where relevant, and archives. Preserve dates.

tasks.name: Normalize claims and capabilities
tasks.objective: Map comparable capabilities, packaging, pricing units, customer segments, distribution, integrations, service levels, and constraints. Do not compare marketing labels as equivalent features.

tasks.name: Model buyer alternatives
tasks.objective: Analyze jobs-to-be-done, switching costs, triggers, blockers, perceived risk, proof requirements, and reasons to win or lose.

tasks.name: Infer strategic moves cautiously
tasks.objective: Identify plausible direction from repeated evidence such as hiring, roadmap signals, acquisitions, partnerships, and pricing changes. Label inference and retain alternatives.

tasks.name: Red-team the picture
tasks.objective: Challenge stale evidence, survivorship bias, review-site distortion, regional differences, custom enterprise deals, false equivalence, and internally convenient narratives.

tasks.name: Publish decision-oriented brief
tasks.objective: Deliver comparison by decision-relevant dimension, source dates, confidence, customer implications, watch indicators, and unknowns without declaring an overall winner.
